data.title: Asteatotic eczema — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Asteatotic eczema** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. Synonyms and definition?**
- Eczema craquelé, xerotic eczema, winter itch — eczema arising on very dry skin from loss of stratum corneum lipids and water

**Q2. Clinical features?**
- Dry, scaly skin with fine fissures in a 'crazy paving' / dried river-bed pattern with erythema, mainly shins of elderly, worse in winter; itchy

**Q3. Predisposing factors?**
- Old age (reduced sebum and natural moisturising factor), low humidity/winter, frequent hot baths and soaps, diuretics, statins, retinoids, hypothyroidism, malnutrition/zinc deficiency, renal failure, malignancy (widespread sudden onset — lymphoma)

**Q4. Differential diagnosis?**
- Stasis dermatitis, nummular eczema, ichthyosis vulgaris/acquired ichthyosis, contact dermatitis, scabies (elderly), cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

**Q5. Treatment?**
- Short lukewarm baths, soap substitutes, liberal emollients immediately after bathing (petrolatum, urea, lactic acid), humidify room
- Mild–moderate topical steroid ointment for inflamed areas for 1–2 weeks; treat itch; stop offending drugs

**Q6. When should you suspect an internal cause?**
- Sudden generalised asteatotic eczema in an adult — screen for lymphoma, malignancy, hypothyroidism, nutritional deficiency

## Quick spotter facts
- Crazy-paving dry fissured shins of an elderly person in winter — asteatotic eczema

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Asteatotic eczema); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.24. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
